olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $k_1<k_2<\cdots$ be positive integers, no two consecutive, and $s_m=k_1+\cdots+k_m$. Prove that for each $n$, the interval $[s_n,s_{n+1})$ contains at least one perfect square.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1994

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A 99-gon has sides colored red, blue, ..., yellow alternately. Can a sequence of single-side recolorings (no two adjacent sides same color) transform the initial coloring to one shifted by two?
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1994

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Cyclic hexagon $ABCDEF$ with $AB=CD=EF$ and concurrent $AD,BE,CF$. Let $P=AD\cap CE$. Prove $CP/PE=(AC/CE)^2$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1994

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $a_j>0$ with $\sum_{j=1}^n a_j\geq\sqrt{n}$ for all $n\geq 1$. Prove $\sum_{j=1}^n a_j^2>\frac{1}{4}\left(1+\frac{1}{2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{n}\right)$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1994

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $S$ be a finite set of positive integers with $|U|,\sigma(U),\pi(U)$ denoting size, sum, product. Prove $\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|U|}\binom{m-\sigma(U)}{|S|}=\pi(S)$ for all integers $m\geq\sigma(S)$.
source: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad 1994
